sections.what_happened: Ukrainian drones struck the Kinef refinery in Kirishi (Russia's second-largest, ~20M metric tonnes/yr, >6% of Russia's refined output, Surgutneftegas, sanctioned) overnight Nov 8-9. Fire erupted; primary oil-processing unit ELOU-AVT-2 caught fire, ELOU-AVT-6 and ELOU-AT-6 also hit (Ukrainska Pravda, citing monitoring channels + ASTRA OSINT). NASA FIRMS detected multiple hotspots at the facility at 04:00 local (Militarnyi; Kyiv Independent). Leningrad governor Aleksandr Drozdenko confirmed the attack on Telegram: fire since extinguished; 113 Ukrainian drones downed over the region; a woman killed in Vsevolozhsk when drone debris hit a residential roof; an apartment in Kirishi damaged. TASS earlier reported 81 drones downed while the air-defence operation was still under way -- timing artifact, not a contradiction. Context: refinery previously hit May 5 (three of four crude distillation units damaged, processing halted) and Aug 30; March attack halted operations completely. Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian energy infrastructure after a temporary halt urged by Trump. The strike lands the night before US-mediated Russia-Ukraine working-level talks open in Abu Dhabi Nov 10-11.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct publisher families: Kyiv Independent (T2), Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA), ANI wire (T1, via Tribune India / New Kerala). Ukrainska Pravda and Militarnyi add unit-level detail but are NOT in the registry and do not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: Russian Defence Ministry claims 430 Ukrainian drones downed over 14 regions + Crimea overnight (already in 1500-04; unverified aggregate). AJ notes it could not independently verify some claims. Scale of damage and any disruption to operations remain unclear (AnewZ). TASS's earlier 81-downed figure vs the governor's later 113 -- explained by timing (operation still under way when TASS reported).
sections.why_matters: Ukraine just torched Russia's SECOND-biggest refinery -- 800 km from the front, the night before the Abu Dhabi talks. Three of its four distillation units were already damaged in May. How much refining can Russia lose before the fuel runs short?
